claim: If a contract admits a value the instruction forbids, that is a gap — recorded even when no artifact has ever sent such a value.

steps.label: a contract that rejects every forbidden value

request.contract: string, min length 1, must contain non-whitespace

steps.label: a contract that only checks length
steps.note: RS-109 holds because the empty string is rejected. RS-111 does not, because whitespace sails through — and nothing about today's traffic would tell you that.

steps.label: every real value passes, and the gap is reported anyway

request.real traffic: 'summarize the repo', 'list the toy paths', 'explain the tests'

steps.result: all real traffic accepted: True; gaps: ['RS-109', 'RS-111']
steps.evidence: the audit takes a contract and rules — there is nowhere to pass a sample
steps.note: The most comfortable failure there is. Every sample passes, every test is green, and the only thing holding the line is that nobody has yet sent the empty string the schema has always accepted.

steps.label: a rule that forbids nothing
steps.note: It cannot be violated, so a contract cannot fail it, so declaring it proves nothing.

steps.label: auditing a contract against no rules at all
steps.detail: a contract audited against nothing passes
